title: Choose the visual world for the ita-rag-bench leaderboard
question: The roll assigned the Official Timetable direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Official Timetable
options.lineage: Italian railway timetables (Orario ufficiale FS, Orario Pozzi)
options.thesis: Every pipeline configuration is a train on a timetable: its stops are parser, chunker, embedding and retrieval, and the timetable shows how much recall is still on board at each stop.
options.viewport: Blue masthead with the run and its validity date; three conclusions in plain words in the reading column; below, the timetable: stages as rows, configurations as columns, recall remaining at each stage, the best train highlighted in yellow marker.
options.risk: A dense grid can intimidate decision makers if the plain-language conclusions above it are not given room.

raised.raise: One highlight per table, never more: the yellow marker means 'the answer to your question'.
Uncertainty is a mark, not a colour: timetable footnote symbols flag draft data and overlapping confidence intervals.
Every configuration gets a train-number code (e.g. PM·ST·BGE) used identically in tables, charts and text.
Conclusions annotate the data and never replace it: every finding points to the rows that prove it.
Each run is a dated sheet: 'valid from 26 October 2026', with earlier runs one link away.

regions.label: blue masthead · run, validity date, IT/EN

options.label: Comparative Test
options.lineage: consumer test magazines (comparison tables, 'best in test' seals)
options.thesis: The benchmark as a consumer test: configurations are products, each judged on quality, cost and speed, with a 'best in test' and a 'best value'.
options.viewport: Verdict up top with the 'best in test' seal; the comparison table below with rating dots per criterion and a verdict row.
options.risk: The most familiar format for buyers, and the one that most invites overstating small differences as wins.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: The pipeline drawn as a building in section: recall enters like daylight and each stage is an aperture that lets some of it through.
options.viewport: One long section across the page; the light band narrows stage by stage; annotations pinned to each loss.
options.case: Shows where recall is lost better than any table, but decision makers do not read architectural sections by habit.
options.risk: The metaphor needs a caption to be understood.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.thesis: Results explained like a friend sketching on a napkin.
options.viewport: Comic panels walking through the findings.
options.case: Undercuts the authority buyers need to cite the numbers.
options.risk: Reads as unserious next to legal documents.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Configurations as frames on a perforated rail.
options.viewport: A rail of frames across the page.
options.case: Film editing is foreign to the audience; the rail hides the comparison.
options.kept: Uncertainty is a mark, not a colour.

options.label: Box Stacks
options.thesis: Each configuration a labelled box on a wall.
options.case: Browsing boxes buries the comparison the reader came for.
options.kept: A consistent code labels every configuration.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: The data as terrain, the findings as a course over it.
options.viewport: A map of results with a purple course.
options.kept: Conclusions annotate the data, never replace it.

options.label: Calendar Pad
options.thesis: Each run a torn-off leaf below a painted plate.
options.viewport: A plate above a date grid.
options.case: Kitsch for an evidence page; lands in the cream-and-red default.
options.kept: Each run is a dated sheet.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A machine-learning leaderboard: one sortable table with heat-coloured cells and a model card, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Title, filter chips, one big sortable table, method below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other leaderboard; hides the pipeline story.
